questions.name: Meenakshi Amman (Green)
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: The tutelary goddess of Madurai, an avatar of Parvati, depicted with green skin and holding a parrot on her shoulder. The famous Madurai Meenakshi Temple celebrates a massive annual festival reenacting her celestial wedding (Meenakshi Tirukalyanam) to Lord Shiva (Sundareswarar).

questions.name: Ananthasayana Vishnu (Ranganatha) / Reclining Deity
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A black stone-style sculpture depicting a reclining deity resting on a serpent bed. In South Indian temples like Srirangam, Vishnu reclines on the multi-headed serpent Adi Shesha, symbolizing calm awareness amidst the cosmic ocean of creation.

questions.name: Radha & Krishna
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: Lord Krishna playing his flute alongside Radha, with a small reclining baby Krishna resting playfully at their feet. Their pairing represents the union of the individual soul (Jivatma) with the divine (Paramatma), a central theme of Bhakti poetry.

questions.name: Rama Darbar (Hanuman, Sita, Rama, Lakshmana)
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A classic set of four dolls from the epic Ramayana: Lord Hanuman standing in devotion, Goddess Sita, Lord Rama holding his bow (Kodanda), and his loyal brother Lakshmana. Navaratri coincides with the celebration of Rama's victory over Ravana (Vijayadashami), making the Rama Darbar one of the most auspicious centerpieces on the top tier of a Golu.

questions.name: Garuda / Brass Deity Figurine
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: An ornate winged brass figurine placed in front of the Rama Darbar. Brass idols (often passed down across generations as family heirlooms) are frequently integrated alongside clay and papier-mâché Golu dolls.

questions.name: Saraswati (Standing with Veena)
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: The Hindu goddess of knowledge, music, arts, and wisdom, playing the traditional South Indian veena. The final three days of Navaratri are dedicated to Saraswati Puja, when books, musical instruments, and tools are placed near the Golu to be blessed.

questions.name: Andal
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: The only female saint among the twelve Alvars (poet-saints of South India), depicted here in an orange-red sari with heavy garlands and a tall crown. Her Tamil devotional poem, the Thiruppavai (30 stanzas), is sung every morning during the Tamil month of Margazhi.

questions.name: Goddess Parvati / Karumari Amman
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A tall, crowned four-armed form of the Divine Mother with lotus-like hands and a trident behind her. Because Navaratri celebrates the feminine divine (Shakti), placing a prominent Amman doll on the highest step anchors the spiritual theme of the display.

questions.name: Ornate Brass Diya (Oil Lamp)
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A decorative brass oil lamp with an arched ornamental backing, flanked by silver Kuthu Vilakku lamps on the top shelf. Lighting lamps around the Golu every evening invites auspiciousness before neighbors gather to sing devotional songs and exchange tamboolam.

questions.name: Ashta Lakshmi Set (With Padmavati & Saraswati)
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A complete row dedicated to the Eight Forms of Goddess Lakshmi (Ashta Lakshmi) seated on lotuses, flanked by an additional Devi on the far left and Goddess Saraswati on the far right. Ashta Lakshmi represents the eight distinct sources of wealth: spirituality (Adi), food/harvest (Dhanya), courage (Dhairya), sovereignty/elephants (Gaja), progeny (Santana), victory (Vijaya), knowledge (Vidya), and monetary prosperity (Dhana).

questions.name: Gaja Lakshmi
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: The centerpiece of the second row, showing Goddess Lakshmi seated on a lotus and flanked by two white elephants holding pink lotuses. Gaja Lakshmi symbolizes royal power, abundance, and the fertility brought by monsoon rains (historically associated with clouds and elephants).

questions.name: Santana Lakshmi
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A multi-armed form of Goddess Lakshmi seated on a lotus with a child on her lap, representing the wealth of family, healthy children, and lineage.

questions.name: Dashavatara Set (Ten Avatars of Vishnu)
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: The back row of the third tier displays the ten primary incarnations of Lord Vishnu spanning cosmic history, including Matsya (fish), Kurma (tortoise), Varaha (boar), Narasimha (half-man/half-lion), Vamana, Parashurama, Rama, Balarama, Krishna, and Kalki/Hayagriva. Many commentators note a striking parallel between the Dashavatara sequence and biological evolution: starting in water, moving to amphibians and land mammals, and developing into human societies.

questions.name: Bhakti Saints & Poet-Musicians
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A cluster of revered poet-saints in front of the Dashavatara, including a seated sage in yellow robes and standing saint-musicians holding string instruments (tambura/veena) and hand cymbals. Saint-composers like Purandara Dasa and Tyagaraja shaped the devotional traditions of Carnatic music commonly sung in front of the Golu.

questions.name: Vithoba (Vitthala) and Rakhumai
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: Lord Vitthala (a form of Krishna worshipped in Pandharpur, Maharashtra) standing in his iconic hands-on-hips posture alongside his consort Rakhumai (Rukmini) in a green sari. According to legend, Vitthala stood waiting with his hands on his hips for his devotee Pundalik, who asked the Lord to wait while he finished serving his elderly parents.

questions.name: Folk Musicians, Dancers & Village Scene
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A lively village scene featuring miniature folk musicians playing drums and string instruments, festive dancers, and a central devotional vignette on a checkered platform. The bottom tiers of a traditional Golu transition from gods and saints to everyday human life, community festivities, and cultural arts—reflecting the cosmic hierarchy.

questions.name: Lord Ganesha Idols
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A large four-armed standing Ganesha alongside a smaller seated Ganesha playing a drum. Even before setting up the Golu steps on Mahalaya Amavasya, a small Ganesha (often made of turmeric) is worshipped first to ensure the festival proceeds without obstacles.

questions.name: Carved Elephant Parade
questions.prompt: Which doll or set is highlighted on the Golu?
questions.explanation: A collection of intricately carved wooden and stone-finished elephants of varying sizes arranged in a family procession. In Indian tradition, elephants symbolize royalty, wisdom, and good luck; displaying an odd or graduated number of animal figurines adds visual harmony to the base of the Golu.
